doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Buddy Rich, Alvino Rey and Manhattan School
title: Walking through Central Park and the modulations
summary: Mandel recalls working out the ending while walking through Central Park, and Kirchner traces the chart's modulations.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I remember one thing about that chart, I spent a lot of time on it, but I figured out the whole last part of it when I was walking through Central Park, after getting off work. In those days, in 1947 you could walk through Central Park at four or five in the morning and I figured that whole ending out as I was walking through where the cross-town traffic goes. By the time I got to the other end of the park I had it figured, all I had to do was go home and write it.
Because just the modulations alone, you start out in D-flat, eight bars later you modulate to G.
And then finish the first chorus in G. And then you go through a whole series of modulations, you go up to C then chromatically C, D flat, D, E flat, E.

And then that takes you half way to the second part of the bridge and the melody note is E and the chord is A-minor, which puts you back in the original key of D flat. And then you modulated G flat and then finally modulated again and finish the chart in F.
I know I finished it in F.
I sat down about a year ago and just consciously figured this out and it took me a while to just find out exactly what you were doing, but once I did, it was just like, ‘Jesus!’
